claims.text: Not recommended with factor IX complex concentrates or anti-inhibitor coagulant concentrates: thrombosis risk may be increased.
claims.quote: Tranexamic acid tablets are not recommended in patients taking either Factor IX complex concentrates or anti-inhibitor coagulant concentrates because the risk of thrombosis may be increased
claims.locator: 7 Drug Interactions › 7.3 Factor IX Complex Concentrates or Anti-Inhibitor Coagulant Concentrates

claims.text: Tissue plasminogen activators may decrease the efficacy of both drugs; stop tranexamic acid if tPA is needed.
claims.quote: Concomitant therapy with tissue plasminogen activators may decrease the efficacy of both tranexamic acid tablets and tissue plasminogen activators. Discontinue tranexamic acid tablets if a patient requires tissue plasminogen activators.

claims.text: Retinal venous and arterial occlusion have been reported.
claims.quote: Retinal venous and arterial occlusion have been reported in patients using tranexamic acid tablets.

claims.text: Report visual or eye symptoms promptly; if they occur, stop it at once and get a complete eye exam from an ophthalmologist.
claims.quote: Patients should be instructed to report visual and ocular symptoms promptly. In the event of such symptoms, patients should be instructed to discontinue tranexamic acid tablets immediately and should be referred to an ophthalmologist for a complete ophthalmic evaluation

claims.text: Renal impairment: lower dose (mostly excreted unchanged in urine).
claims.quote: Because tranexamic acid is primarily eliminated via the kidneys by glomerular filtration with more than 95% excreted as unchanged in urine, the recommended dosage in patients with renal impairment is lower than the recommended dosage in patients with normal renal function
claims.locator: 8 Use in Specific Populations › 8.6 Renal Impairment
